text:
alice (SRE): Alert: us-west-2 hosted-api showing ~18% 503s since 08:34. Upstream runner processes on pool 'auth-heavy' are aborting; saw CUDA abort / coredump on node i-0abc. Affected customer ACME reporting timeouts and increased billing/retries.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished 2025-03-18T08:22:14Z — service/runner v2.14 -> v2.15 on pool 'auth-heavy' (job 7503).

ben (oncall): looking into logs now. matt, did we change anything on that pool overnight?

matt (runtime): we enabled kv_prefetch=true for quantized variants in that pool last night to reduce tail latency. I saw a handful of OOM-ish warnings in staging but it passed. pushing relevant logs below.

matt (runtime): ```
[runner][FATAL] 2025-03-18T08:34:37Z runtime abort: cuda runtime error: out of memory
Backtrace:
  0x7f8a12ab handler.c:321
  0x7f8b33ef kv_prefetch.c:88
  0x7f8b44aa inference.c:210
```

lucy (support): CS: ACME says they get 500/503 on single-request generation (no toolcall). Errors started ~08:34 and persisted ~12 mins. They also saw duplicate charge events for retried calls. They want ETA and whether requests were retried server-side.

ben (oncall): quick repro I ran: send a single large context (~50k tokens) + 4 concurrent streams to hosted-api in us-west; within ~20s the worker OOMs and container restarts. curl example: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate`

alice (SRE): Collectors: grab core + nvml + journal. Commands: `sudo journalctl -u runner -n 500 --no-pager`, `ls /var/crash | grep core.runner`, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=mem_used --format=csv -l 1` on the node i-0abc. Upload to INC-9753.

matt (runtime): Proposed mitigation: disable kv_prefetch on auth-heavy and roll back runner -> v2.14. The prefetch path seems to cause fragmentation under quantized kernels, leading to cudaMalloc failures then abort. Do we want immediate rollback or toggle flag?

ben (oncall): rollback now. If rollback takes >5m enable fallback routing to smaller-quant model in us-west until patch is verified. I'll trigger rollback and routing rule.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated 2025-03-18T08:39:05Z — service/runner reverting to v2.14 on pool 'auth-heavy' (job 7521).

alice (SRE): :thumbsup: Ben -> coordinate CS notification to ACME. @cs_acme please confirm receipt.

cs_acme: ACME -> Confirmed. We saw failures and duplicate events 08:34-08:46; please advise on refunds and root cause.

lucy (support): I'll open billing ticket and put in temporary credit for duplicated/failed calls. Also advising ACME to stop client-side retries for now.

ben (oncall): Initial hypothesis: prefetch + large-context on quantized kernels -> allocator fragmentation -> cudaMalloc fail -> abort/segfault. Repro steps for engineering: 1) kv_prefetch=on for quant models, 2) send ~50k token request x4 concurrent, 3) watch for `cudaMalloc` failure and runner exit.

matt (runtime): I'll push the targeted rollback and a hotfix: add allocator guard (if cudaMalloc fails twice within 30s mark pool unhealthy) + autoscaler rule to route away from pool after 3 coredumps in 10m. Also adding metrics for cudaAlloc failures.

alice (SRE): Good. Attach cores + nvml logs to ticket INC-9753. Assign root cause to @matt (runtime). We'll run heap analysis for fragmentation and test on staging with quantized builds.

ben (oncall): CS: message to ACME: rolled back runner, routing fallbacks enabled, refunding duplicate calls. ETA for RCA: 24h.

cs_acme: Thanks — please send a postmortem and assign ownership for follow-ups.

lucy (support): ack

notes (ben): follow-ups: 1) revert prefetch default for quantized models in prod pools until verified; 2) add guardrails in runtime to avoid abort on allocation failures; 3) run long soak tests with large contexts on quant builds.

-- end of thread --
